A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MeanFlow training work. All 15 pages in each version, including Appendices A–C, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments and controlled velocity-learning studies in Sections 4 and 6, plus FFHQ experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ImageNet experiments, velocity-learning analyses, and FFHQ results, including the component ablation in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix B retain the same velocity-acceleration techniques, progressive temporal-gap loss weighting, and integration objectives. No algorithmic or architectural change is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet 256×256 class-conditional generation and FFHQ unconditional generation, with the same observational and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same MeanFlow, iCT, Shortcut, iMM, and other generative-model comparisons. Comparator membership in the CFG and component-ablation experiments also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The DiT configurations, 240-epoch ImageNet comparisons, 50K-sample FID evaluation, NFE settings, CFG configurations, and appendix experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The velocity-pretraining, corruption, temporal-gap, task-affinity, CFG robustness, component-ablation, and schedule-sensitivity analyses are retained. Appendix C contains the same FFHQ studies and ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The task-affinity sampling and averaging procedure in Appendix A is unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported scores, plotted trends, and generated examples match. For example, both Table 1 versions report 1-NFE FIDs of 3.43 for MeanFlow-XL/2 and 2.87 with the proposed DTD-based training; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The Flow Matching and MeanFlow definitions, objectives, progressive-weighting formulas, and Appendix B equations are mathematically unchanged. Equation reflow adds no definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about velocity-learning dependencies, improved few-step generation, and faster convergence, including the approximately 2.5× training-speedup claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of large-gap supervision destabilizing instantaneous velocity and MinSNR interacting with adaptive loss weighting remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Implementation information in Section 6.1, experimental details in Appendix A, integration instructions in Appendix B, and the code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: All 87 references are retained unchanged after matching bibliography page breaks. Research positioning, including the comparisons with AlphaFlow and CMT, is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Yonsei University and Max Planck ETH CLS affiliations and a funding/support acknowledgment before the references. It also removes the word 'score' from one sentence in Section 4.3; the scientific narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: On page 8, Table 4 moves from the right column to below Table 3 in the left column, while Table 5 moves upward. Table 4's caption is shortened and restyled, and equations, paragraphs, and references reflow. Figures and appendix pages remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds institutional and funding attribution and makes limited wording and layout edits. The scientific explanations, experimental evidence, results, and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
